mainVideo.title: Let's Learn English Level 2 Lesson 29: Where There's Smoke...

transcript.speaker: PENELOPE
transcript.text: Hey, Anna. What are you reading?

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: I’m reading about fire safety. Ms. Weaver named me fire safety monitor.

transcript.speaker: PENELOPE
transcript.text: But the only time we have a fire emergency is when someone burns a piece of toast.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: That is true. But fire safety is very serious – very serious. If there is a fire emergency, I have to help everyone out of the building.

transcript.speaker: PENELOPE
transcript.text: Well then, if I were you, I’d learn as much as possible.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: You’re right. And I know just who to call!

transcript.speaker: PROF. BOT
transcript.text: Hmm, I wonder where Anna’s going. Today we are reviewing conditionals and learning helpful language for emergencies.

transcript.speaker: PROF. BOT
transcript.text: If Anna studies hard, she’ll be a great fire safety monitor! That’s a conditional. It uses “if” to show that something is true only when something else is true.

transcript.speaker: PROF. BOT
transcript.text: Let’s find out where Anna is going. And if you want to learn fire emergency language, keep watching!
(Two firefighters welcome Anna to their firehouse.)

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: Hi, Firefighter Jones.

transcript.speaker: FIREFIGHTER JONES
transcript.text: Hey, how are you, Anna?

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: I’m well, thanks. How are you? Hi, Firefighter Hatcher.

transcript.speaker: FIREFIGHTER HATCHER
transcript.text: Hi, Anna. How are you?

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: I’m well, thanks.

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: Welcome to our firehouse.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: Come on in.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: This is where the firefighters eat. This is where we rest. This is where we exercise. This is where the firetrucks are parked and maintained.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: This place is beautiful.

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: You know, the firehouse is a firefighter’s second home.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: Firefighter Jones, Firefighter Hatcher: Can you tell me some ways to prepare for a fire emergency?

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: Sure, Anna. There’s one really important thing you can do: Install a fire alarm. Test it monthly and make sure the batteries are fully charged.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: Let’s talk about those emergency exits.

transcript.speaker: FF J
transcript.text: In your home, office and schools, know where your emergency exits are located.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: What about fire extinguishers? FF J: Everyone should know how to use a fire extinguisher. Have one handy and practice using it.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: What if we need to get out?

transcript.speaker: FF J
transcript.text: You should have an evacuation plan. And practice getting out safely with fire drills. ANNA: If I am in a building and it’s on fire, should I use the elevator?

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: No. Always use the stairs.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: What other safety tips should I know?

transcript.speaker: FF J
transcript.text: Stay low. Smoke rises. The air is clearer close to the ground.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: Stay low. Anything else?

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: If you touch a door and it’s hot, don’t open it. There might be a fire on the other side.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: What do I do if my clothes catch on fire? FF H: Do not run. If you run, the fire will burn faster. You must stop, drop and roll.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: Thanks so much! I’ve learned a lot. And I can’t wait to share this information with others.

transcript.speaker: FF H
transcript.text: Thanks for coming, Anna.

transcript.speaker: FF J
transcript.text: It’s been a pleasure meeting you.
(Anna is back at the office talking to Penelope.)

transcript.speaker: PENELOPE
transcript.text: So, Anna, how was the visit to the fire station?

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: I learned a lot! And firefighters have a very difficult job.

transcript.speaker: PENELOPE
transcript.text: Do you smell smoke?

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: No. So, like I was saying, I learned how to …

transcript.speaker: PENELOPE
transcript.text: Anna, I smell smoke.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: If you smell smoke, call the fire department!
(Anna begins to evacuate her coworkers.)

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: If you smell smoke, get out of the building. Come on people, we have a fire emergency! Leave your things and evacuate calmly and quickly. Very good. Very good.

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: We have a fire emergency. No, take the stairs Let’s get out. Let’s get out safely.
(Anna and coworkers stand outside of the building.)

transcript.speaker: ANNA
transcript.text: We got out in less than 6 minutes! Good job, people! Wait. Where’s Pete?

transcript.speaker: PENELOPE
transcript.text: I know where he is. I’ll go get him. ANNA: No! Never go back into a burning building! The fire department is coming. Stay calm, Pete. Help is on the way! Help is on the way!
Anna takes her job as fire safety monitor very seriously. She visits a local fire station.

Emergency Language Today, you learned important language to use for fire emergencies. Study and remember them. How many can you remember? Helpful Language Helpful Phrases emergency exit/s evacuation plan firefighter fire extinguisher fire truck firehouse fire station fire department fire drill/s catch fire / catch on fire Install fire alarms. I smell smoke. Do you smell smoke? There’s a fire! Call the fire department! The building is on fire! Stop, drop and roll.

transcript.speaker: Ashley

transcript.speaker: Anna

transcript.speaker: Ashley
transcript.text: Bye, Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Bye, Dublin.

transcript.speaker: Anna

transcript.speaker: Nurse

transcript.speaker: Anna

transcript.speaker: Nurse

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Awesome!

transcript.speaker: Jonathan

transcript.speaker: Anna

transcript.speaker: Jonathan
transcript.text: That’s easy. I’d love to win the World Karaoke Contest.

transcript.speaker: Anna

transcript.speaker: Jonathan
transcript.text: Are you serious? Can you read the story by yourself?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sure, absolutely.

transcript.speaker: Jonathan
transcript.text: Thanks!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You go.
(Anna goes outside and talks to Penelope.)

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Penelope, I was wondering if you still dream of being a dancer.

transcript.speaker: Penelope
transcript.text: Only every day!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, guess what: A famous dancer is having a flash mob around the corner! Hundreds of people are dancing together!

transcript.speaker: Penelope
transcript.text: No way!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Way! If you leave right now, you can join them! Bye!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Pete, what’s one of your dreams?

transcript.speaker: Pete
transcript.text: Well, last night I dreamt I was in a spaceship. I was flying through outer space with these two beautiful...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Pete -- not that kind of dream. I mean your hopes for the future.
Pete Oh. I plan on selling my book to Hollywood and becoming rich and famous.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That’s going to be difficult.

transcript.speaker: Pete

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, good job, Anna! My work here is done … almost.

transcript.speaker: MUSIC
transcript.text: You can search but you won't find the answer without a dream. You can reach for the stars but you won't get there without a dream...without a dream.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Weaver
transcript.text: Anna, what’s going on? Where is everybody?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I don’t know. Maybe something is, uh, going around the office.

transcript.speaker: Anna

transcript.speaker: Ms. Weaver
transcript.text: What did you say, Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna

transcript.text: We hope you have enjoyed Level 2 of Let’s Learn English. Everyone is following their dreams, big and small.
